test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 28 Nov, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Which Article of the Constitution of India mentions that “it shall be the duty of every citizen of India to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women”?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 51A (e)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 51A (e) is part of the Fundamental Duties listed in the Constitution of India.
 
• It specifically emphasizes the duty of every citizen to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood.
 
• This includes transcending religious, linguistic, and regional or sectional diversities.
 
• It also calls upon citizens to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• These duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• They are inspired by the Constitution of the former Soviet Union.
 
• Originally, 10 Fundamental Duties were added, and the 11th was inserted by the 86th Amendment in 2002.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Fundamental Duties**
 
 
• They serve as a constant reminder to citizens about their responsibilities towards the nation.
 
• They help promote a sense of discipline and commitment among citizens.
 
 
 
• **Related Articles**
 
 
• Article 51A (a): To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions.
 
• Article 51A (d): To defend the country and render national service when called upon.
 
• Article 51A (k): To provide opportunities for education to children between the ages of six and fourteen years.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Interpretation**
 
 
• The Supreme Court of India has emphasized the importance of Fundamental Duties in various judgments.
 
• They are considered essential for the proper functioning of the democratic system.
